answer_part:
The CONTROL device formulation includes m-MeO-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL as an additive in the perovskite precursor solution, while m-F-PEACl is absent. Analysis of the CONTROL performance—PCE of 23.606%, Voc of 1.17607 V, Jsc of 25.3513 mA/cm², and FF of 79.1751%—indicates that m-MeO-PEACl is limiting device performance. The methoxy group in m-MeO-PEACl acts as an electron-donating moiety, which provides moderate passivation of undercoordinated Pb²⁺ defects at grain boundaries and interfaces but fails to sufficiently suppress non-radiative recombination. This results in significant voltage losses and reduced charge extraction efficiency, directly contributing to the suboptimal Voc and FF. Specifically, the electron-donating nature weakens the binding strength to Pb²⁺ ions compared to electron-withdrawing alternatives, leaving deep-level traps inadequately passivated. Consequently, increased trap-assisted recombination elevates dark current and lowers the quasi-Fermi level splitting, manifesting as the observed Voc deficit. Additionally, incomplete grain boundary coverage exacerbates ion migration, further degrading FF through hysteresis and series resistance losses.  

Replacing m-MeO-PEACl with m-F-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL addresses these limitations through enhanced defect passivation. The fluorine substituent in m-F-PEACl introduces strong electron-withdrawing character, significantly increasing electronegativity at the binding site. This strengthens the interaction with undercoordinated Pb²⁺ ions, more effectively neutralizing deep traps that drive non-radiative recombination. The improved passivation reduces interfacial and bulk trap density, directly elevating Voc by minimizing Shockley-Read-Hall losses. Simultaneously, the fluorinated compound promotes a more uniform and stable 2D perovskite capping layer at grain boundaries, which suppresses ion migration and enhances hole extraction. This dual action—reduced recombination and improved charge transport—boosts both FF and Jsc. The trade-off of potential over-passivation is mitigated by maintaining the identical concentration (2.0 mg/mL), ensuring optimal surface coverage without impeding charge carrier mobility or inducing excessive insulating character.  

The proposed formulation change yields substantial performance gains. The improved device achieves a PCE in the range of 25.2% to 27.0%, with Voc elevated to 1.17–1.21 V, Jsc increased to 26.31–26.60 mA/cm², and FF enhanced to 81.92–83.92%. These improvements stem directly from the superior defect passivation and interfacial stabilization provided by m-F-PEACl, which collectively minimize recombination pathways and optimize charge collection.
